title: What a packet narrative is meant to say, beside a case whose identifiers could be read into it: amounts, dates (a year, a month and day, or a month's name that is a number or a name of the case), codes, units, an NPI, a plan identifier the facts hold, another person's Social Security- or phone-shaped number, citation markers, identifier placeholders and fact tokens that spell an identifier, a label, a placeholder and then a date, and the words that are a short part of a hyphenated name ("in" beside HYE-IN, "to" beside TO-UYEN); generated narratives of such pieces and of written identifiers; the browser's check
assertion: None of it is read as an identifier, and the code's own draft passes for any case whose identifiers it does not hold; the verifier flags an identifier wherever its whole-word reading or the gateway's narrative reading (`holdsNameOrNumber`, the drafter's check of its facts) holds one outside the tokens and the dated figures, but for a part of a name's word under four letters by itself, and nowhere that neither they nor the reading across a token do; the reading the verifier asks where (`nameOrNumberMatches`) answers as the drafter's check does on any text in its NFKC form that holds none of the gateway's own placeholders (the check normalizes and masks for itself), and leaving an identifier out changes no other's matches; the browser's check loads neither the matcher nor the server's reading
noFileReason: Narratives are generated in memory by the property test from pieces it holds; no file.
